ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y_{1}=x+b$ intersects with the line $y_{2}=kx-1$ at point $P$, where the $x$-coordinate of point $P$ is $-1$. What is the solution set of the inequality $x+b<kx-1$ in terms of $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By observing the graph of the function, it is found that when $x < -1$, the graph of the function $y = x + b$ is below the graph of $y = kx - 1$,\\
therefore, the solution set of the inequality $x + b < kx - 1$ is $x < -1$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{x < -1}$.
